close_reason: Fixed in rm8.65: added as_dns_name, as_ip_bytes, local_part, domain, is_internationalized
description:
Public API surface gap: ServerName<'a> and MailboxName<'a> have private fields and zero accessor methods.

Once parsed:

* No way to read back the normalized DNS A-label form (caller has bücher.example, parses, cannot get xn--bcher-kva.example back out).
* No way to read back the canonical IPv6 bytes or render to dotted/colon form.
* No way to read the mailbox local-part, domain A-label, or is_internationalized flag.

Callers who want to log/audit/serialize the parsed form must:

1. retain the original input string alongside the typed handle, or
2. re-parse and re-stringify themselves, defeating the validate-once point of the type.

Impact (caller-side):

* Logging: only {:?} works, and that exposes the internal Cow variant choice (Borrowed vs Owned), which is implementation-specific and may change.
* Caching/serde: even with the optional serde feature, ServerName / MailboxName don't get Serialize/Deserialize derives — see separate finding. But even with that, the type currently has nothing to serialize *to* shape-wise without exposing private fields.
* Pkix-chain wrapper code in this workspace can't display *which* identity failed validation without keeping a parallel string.

Minimum viable accessor surface (proposed for resolution, not for this filing):

* ServerName::as_dns_str(&self) -> Option<&str>
* ServerName::as_ip_bytes(&self) -> Option<&[u8]>  // already used internally
* ServerName::is_dns(&self) -> bool / is_ip(&self) -> bool
* MailboxName::local_part(&self) -> &str
* MailboxName::domain(&self) -> &str  (A-label form)
* MailboxName::is_internationalized(&self) -> bool

This is a forever commitment if shipped without accessors: adding them later is non-breaking, but the maintainer loses the option of a) reading the normalized form, b) round-tripping for caller-side caches. The non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendly result types) implies these accessors must exist for ValidationPolicy/Verifier caches to work without retaining parallel string copies.

Verdict: callers will write defensive 'keep the original string around' wrappers forever if this ships as-is.
title: ServerName / MailboxName have no public accessors — types are write-only post-parse
